He is my God, my Savior, and my great refuge, so that I will not be shaken.
How long will you attack a man to kill him, like a leaning wall or a fence pushed over?
They even planned to thrust him down from his place of honor, and they rushed into falsehood. With their mouths they bless, but in their hearts they curse.
Wait for God, my soul, for my salvation comes from him.
He is my God, my Savior, and my refuge, so that I will not be shaken.
My salvation and my honor rest with God. God is my strength, my helper, and my hope.
Trust in him at all times, you people, and pour out your hearts before him, for God is our shelter.
All human beings are like a breath, deceptive. On the scales they rise; together they are weightless.
Do not trust in oppression, and do not love plunder. When wealth increases, do not let your heart delight in it.
God has said one thing, and I have heard these two things: that power belongs to God,
and that mercy belongs to you, Lord, for you repay each person according to their deeds.
My God, you are my God; I wait for you. My soul thirsts for you, and my flesh longs for you, like a thirsty, weary land that needs water.
So I have looked upon you in truth, to see your power and your glory.
For your mercy is better than life, and my lips will praise you.
So I will bless you throughout my life, and in your name I will lift up my hands.
My soul will be richly nourished as with fat and rich food, and my mouth will praise you with lips of praise.
I remembered you on my bed, and during the nights I meditated on you.
For you have been my helper, and in the shadow of your wings I will glory.
My soul went after you, and your right hand rested upon me.
Those who sought to destroy my life will enter the depths of the earth.
They will be handed over to the sword and become food for foxes.
But the king will rejoice in God, and everyone who swears by him will boast, for the mouths of liars will be shut.
Hear my voice, God, as I plead with you, and protect me from the terror of my enemies.
Hide me from the wrongdoing of the wicked and from the activity of those who do evil.
They sharpened their tongues like a sword, and their words like an arrow,
to shoot at the blameless person in secret. Suddenly they will shoot at him and will not be seen.
They strengthened their evil purpose and plotted to hide traps, saying, “Who sees us?”
They plotted injustices and continued to search out evil from within a person and from the depths of his heart.
God will be exalted and will suddenly shoot an arrow at them.
Their tongues will grow weak, and everyone who sees them will be afraid.
All people will be afraid and will proclaim God's deeds, and they will consider the work of his hands.
The righteous will rejoice in the Lord and trust in him, and all the upright in heart will praise him.
Praise is fitting for you, God, in Zion, and vows are fulfilled to you.
Hear my prayer; all flesh will come to you.
Words of wickedness are stronger than I am, but you will forgive my sins.
Blessed is the one you favor and bring near to live in your courts. We will be satisfied with the good things of your house and the holiness of your temple.
In your awesome righteousness, answer me, God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of distant nations.
He establishes the mountains by his strength and strengthens himself with his might.
He stills the storms of the seas and the sound of their waves. The nations will be troubled.
The inhabitants of the earth will be afraid at your signs, and at the coming of morning and evening, with praise.
You remembered the earth and gave it rest; you enriched it abundantly. God's watercourses are full of water. You prepared their food when you prepared the earth.
You soaked its furrows so that its fruits might grow. It will flourish with showers, and its growth will be blessed.
Bless the crown of the year with your goodness, and your calves will have their fill of tender grass.
They will have their fill from the pastures in the wilderness, and the hills will gird themselves with praise.
The fat sheep will clothe themselves, and the valleys will be filled with grain. They will rejoice and give praise.
Praise God, all the earth!
Sing to the glory of his name; sing to the glory of his praise.
Say to God, “How awesome are your deeds! Because of your great strength, your enemies will be enrolled as yours.”
Throughout the earth they will worship you, sing to you, and praise your name forever.
They will say, “Come and see the deeds of God, whose wonders toward humanity are many.”
He turned the sea into dry land, and they crossed the river on foot. There we will rejoice in him.
He rules by his might forever. His eyes watch the nations, and the rebellious will never exalt themselves.
Bless God, you nations, and hear the sound of his praise.
He has kept us alive and has not allowed our feet to slip.
For you tested us, God, and refined us as silver is refined.
You brought us into a trap and laid affliction on our backs.
You made a man ride over our heads. You brought us into fire and water, and you brought us out into relief.
I will come to your house with honor and fulfill my vows to you:
what my lips uttered through the speech of my mouth when I was in distress.
I will offer you fat burnt offerings, with the fat of rams; I will sacrifice bulls and goats.
Come, listen, all you servants of God, and I will tell you what he has done for me.
With my mouth I called to him, and he answered me; I exalted him with my tongue.
If I have seen wickedness in my heart, do not save me, Lord.
Then God heard the sound of my plea.
Blessed is the Lord, who has not turned away my prayer or his grace from me.
May our God have mercy on us and bless us, and make his face shine upon us,
so that we may know his ways on earth and his salvation among all nations.
Let the peoples thank you, God; let all the peoples thank you.
Let the kingdoms rejoice and give praise, because you judge the peoples justly and guide the kingdoms on earth.
Let the peoples thank you, God; let all the peoples thank you.
The earth has yielded its fruit. May God, our God, bless us.
May God bless us, and may all the ends of the earth fear him.
Let God arise, and let all his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee from his presence.
As smoke vanishes, let them vanish; as wax melts before fire, let the wicked perish before God.
The righteous will rejoice and grow strong before God, and they will rejoice in his delight.
Sing to God and praise his name. Praise the one who rides to the west; the Lord is his name. Be strong before him.
For God in his holy dwelling is the father of orphans and the judge of widows.
God settles the lonely in a home and brings prisoners out into prosperity, but the rebellious will dwell among the tombs.
God, when you went out before your people, when you passed through the wilderness,
The earth shook, and the heavens also dripped before God—this Mount Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.
you freely gave rain, God, to your inheritance. It had grown weak, and you strengthened it.
Your creatures dwell in it. In your goodness you strengthened the needy, God.
The Lord will give the message of good news with great power.
The kings of armies will gather, and the beauty of your house will divide the plunder.
If you lie down among the sheepfolds—the wings of a dove covered with silver, and its feathers with gleaming gold.
When God appointed a king over it, it was covered with snow in Zalmon.
The mountain of God, the mountains of Bashan; many-peaked mountains, the mountains of Bashan.
What do you want with the mountains of Gabnim? This is the mountain God chose to dwell in; the Lord will dwell in it forever.
The chariots of God are in myriads and mighty thousands. The Lord is among them; Sinai is in his sanctuary.
You ascended on high and took captives; you gave gifts to human beings. But rebels will not dwell before God.
Blessed is the Lord every day, who chose us as his inheritance—God our Savior, God our deliverer.
The Lord God is master of the way out of death.
But God will split the heads of his enemies, the hairy crowns of those who walk in their sins.
The Lord said, “I will bring them out of Beth-shan, and I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,
so that your foot may be dipped in blood, and the tongues of your dogs may have blood from your enemies.”
They have seen your processions, God, the processions of my God and my holy King.
The princes went ahead, with the singers behind, among young women playing tambourines.
In the assemblies bless the Lord God, you who come from the springs of Israel.
There is little Benjamin in silence, the leaders of Judah and their rulers, the leaders of Zebulun and the leaders of Naphtali.
Command your strength, God; strengthen, God, what you have prepared for us.
From your temple in Jerusalem, kings will bring offerings to you.
Rebuke the beast of the reeds, the herd of bulls, the calves of the peoples that are covered with silver. Scatter the peoples who desire war.
Envoys will come from Egypt, and Cush will stretch out its hand in submission to God.
Kingdoms of the earth, praise God; sing to the Lord,
who rides in the highest heavens from the east. He gives forth his voice, a mighty voice.
Give praise to God; and Israel [?] the greatness of the splendor of his strength is in the highest heavens.
You are awesome, God, from your sanctuary. The God of Israel will give strength and might to his people. Blessed is God!
Save me, God, for the waters have reached my very life.
I have sunk into a deep pit, where there is no place to stand. I have entered the depths of the waters, and the torrent has submerged me.
I am weary from calling out, and my throat is parched. My eyes have failed while I wait for my God.
My enemies without cause are more numerous than the hairs of my head; my false enemies are stronger than my bones. I was made to repay what I had not stolen.
God, you know my foolish deeds, and my sins are not hidden from you.
Do not let those who hope in you be ashamed because of me, Lord God Almighty. Do not let those who seek you be disgraced because of me, God of Israel.
Because of you I have endured insults, and shame has covered my face.
I have become a stranger to my brothers, a foreigner to my mother's sons.
For zeal for your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
I humbled myself with fasting, and I became an object of scorn to them.
I made sackcloth my clothing, and I became a byword to them.
Those who sit at the gate talked about me, and those who drink strong drink talked about me.
But I prayed before you, Lord, at an acceptable time. God, in the abundance of your kindness answer me, and in the abundance of your salvation.
Rescue me from the mud so that I do not sink. Let me escape from those who hate me and from the deep waters.
Do not let the floodwaters drown me, or the abyss swallow me, or the pit close its mouth over me.
Answer me, Lord, for your kindness is good; turn toward me in your abundant mercy.
Do not turn your face away from your servant. Because I am in distress, answer me quickly.
Bring my soul near to your salvation; save me because of my enemies.
You know my disgrace and my shame before all my enemies.
Heal my broken heart and bind it up. I waited for someone who would care, but there was no one, and for a comforter, but I found none.
They put bitter things in my food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Let their table before them become a trap, and their reward a stumbling block.
Let their eyes grow dark so that they cannot see, and let their backs always be bent.
Pour out your anger on them, and let your burning wrath overtake them.
Let their dwelling place be desolate, and let no one live in their tents.
For they persecuted the one you struck, and added to the pain of the slain man.
Add guilt to their guilt, so that they may not enter into your righteousness.
Let them be erased from your book of life, and let them not be recorded with your righteous people.
But I am poor and in pain. Help me, God, with your salvation.
I will praise God's name with a song of praise and magnify him with thanksgiving.
I will please the Lord more than fattened bulls with horns and hooves.
Look, you poor, and rejoice, and let your hearts live.
For the Lord hears the poor and does not despise his prisoners.
Let heaven and earth praise him, the seas and everything that moves in them.
For God will save Zion and rebuild the towns of Judah, so that his servants may live there and possess it.
Those who love his name will dwell there.
God, rescue me! Lord, hurry to help me!
Let those who seek my life be ashamed and disgraced. Let those who wish me harm turn back in disgrace.
Let those who said of me, “Aha, aha!” be stunned by their repeated shame.
Let all who seek you rejoice in you, and let those who love your salvation always say, “God is great!”
But I am poor and afflicted. God, hurry to me! You are my helper and my rescuer. My God, do not delay!
In you, Lord, I have placed my hope. Let me never be put to shame.
In your righteousness, rescue me. Turn your ear toward me and save me.
Be a dwelling place for me, where I can enter at any time. Give the command to save me, for you are my refuge and my fortress.
God, rescue me from the hand of the wicked, from the hand of the evil wrongdoer.
For you are my hope, Lord God, my confidence since my youth.
I have leaned on you since the womb. Since I was in my mother's womb, you have been my confidence. I have praised you continually.
I have become a wonder to many, for you are my strong support.
Let my mouth be filled with your praise and with your greatness all day long.
Do not cast me away in old age, and when my strength is exhausted, do not abandon me.
For my enemies have spoken against me, and those who watch for my life have plotted together.
They have said, “God has abandoned him. Pursue him and seize him, for he has no rescuer.”
God, do not be far from me. God, hurry to help me!
Let those who oppose my life be ashamed and disgraced. Let those who wish me harm be wrapped in shame.
But I will pray continually and add to your praises.
My mouth will proclaim your righteousness and speak your praises all day long, for I have no learning.
I will enter in the Lord's strength, and I alone will recount your righteousness.
God, you have been my instruction since my youth, and to this day I declare your wonders.
Even in old age and advanced years, do not abandon me, until I declare your arm and your might to the coming generation.
Your righteousness, O God, reaches to the heights. You have done great things, O God; who is like you?
You have shown me much distress and trouble, but you have revived me again. You will bring me up again even from the depths of the earth.
You have increased my greatness and comforted me again.
I too will thank you with the harp and sing of your faithfulness, O God. I will sing to you with the harp, Holy One of Israel.
My lips will praise you when I sing to you, and so will my soul, which you have redeemed.
My tongue will acknowledge your righteousness all day long, because those who wish me harm will be ashamed and disgraced.
God, give your judgment to the king, and your righteousness to the king's son.
May he judge your people with righteousness and your poor with justice.
May the mountains bring peace to your people, and the hills your righteousness.
May he defend the poor among the people, save the children of the needy, and bring down the oppressors.
May they fear you as long as the sun lasts, and before the moon, through all generations.
May he come down like rain on a fleece, like showers falling on the earth.
May righteousness flourish in his days, and peace abound until the moon passes away.
May he rule from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the earth.
May the islands bow before him, and may his enemies lick the dust.
May the kings of Tarshish and the islands bring him gifts; may the kings of Sheba and Seba present offerings.
May all kings bow down to him, and may all nations serve him.
For he delivers the needy from those stronger than they are, and the poor who have no helper.
He has compassion on the poor and needy, and saves the lives of the poor.
He redeems their lives from deceit and injustice; their blood is precious in his eyes.
May he live, and may gold from Sheba be given to him. May prayer be offered for him at all times, and may they bless him all day long.
May he be like abundant grain in the land. May his fruit flourish on the mountaintops like Lebanon, and may it spring up from the city like the grass of the earth.
May his name endure forever; his name exists before the sun. May all nations be blessed through him, and may they all praise him.
Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone does great wonders.
Blessed is his glorious name forever. May the whole earth be filled with his glory. Amen and amen.
God is good to Israel and to the pure in heart.
But as for me, my feet had almost slipped; my steps had very nearly given way.
For I envied the wrongdoers when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
For there is no end to their death, and their folly is great.
They do not share in human toil, nor are they afflicted like other people.
Therefore contempt has taken hold of them, and their wrongdoing and wickedness have been concealed.
Their wrongdoing came out like fat, and they acted according to the thoughts of their hearts.
They schemed and spoke evil and oppression; they spoke against the Most High.
They set their mouths in heaven, and their tongues roam the earth.
Therefore my people will return here, and they will find plenty for themselves.
They will say, “How does God know? Is there knowledge in the Most High?”
Look, these wicked people prosper in the world and are mighty in strength.
But I alone purified my heart and washed my hands in purity.
I was afflicted all day long, and my rebuke came in the morning.
If I said that I would act like them,
it is wrongdoing in my eyes.
Until I enter God's sanctuary and consider their end.
You will deal with them according to their deceit, and you will cast them down when they are exalted.
How suddenly they became an object of horror! They perished and were brought to an end by terrors.
Like someone who wakes after seeing a dream, Lord, you will despise their image in the city.
My heart was troubled, and my kidneys were affected.
I was senseless and did not understand; I was like an animal with you.
For you held my right hand.
Comfort me with your counsel, and lead me after your glory.
What do I have in heaven besides you? And what have I desired on earth?
My heart and my flesh have failed; the strength of my heart, my portion, is in God forever.
For look, those far from you will perish, and you will destroy forever all who stray from you.
I have desired to draw near to God; it is good for me. Your name, LORD, is my confidence, so that I may recount all your wonders.
God, why have you forgotten us forever and intensified your anger against the sheep of your pasture?
Remember your congregation, which you acquired long ago and redeemed as the tribe of your inheritance, this Mount Zion where you have dwelt.
Raise your servants by your strength against those who exalt themselves, against all the harm the enemy does to your sanctuary.
Your enemies boasted in the midst of your festival; they set up their own signs as signs.
And you knew [?], like one lifting high, as in a thicket of trees with axes.
They split the doors apart together with hatchets and hammers.
They set your sanctuary on fire and burned it; they defiled the dwelling place of your name, bringing it to the ground.
They said in their hearts, “Let us destroy them together and wipe out all God's festivals from the land.”
They did not see their signs. There is no longer a prophet, nor is there a wise person among us.
How long, God, will the enemy insult you and revile your name forever?
Why have you withdrawn your hand, your right hand, from the midst of your festival?
Our God is the king who brought about deliverance in the midst of the earth.
You divided the sea by your strength and broke the heads of the sea monsters in the waters.
You crushed the heads of Leviathan and gave him as food to a mighty people.
You broke open springs in the valleys; you dried up mighty rivers.
The day is yours, and the night is yours. You established the light and the sun.
You established all the boundaries of the earth; you created summer and winter.
Remember, Lord, the enemy's insults; a foolish people has reviled your name.
Do not hand over to destruction the life that gives you thanks, and do not forget the lives of your poor forever.
Look, Lord, upon your covenant, for the dwelling places of the earth are filled with darkness and injustice.
Do not let the poor return in shame; let the wretched and the poor praise your name.
Rise up, God, and defend your cause. Remember the insults directed at you by fools every day.
Do not forget the voices of your enemies or the uproar of those who rise against you, which goes up continually.
We give thanks to you, God; we give thanks to you. We call on your name and recount all your wonders.
For I will choose a time, and I will judge uprightly.
The earth and all its inhabitants will be brought low; you established its inhabitants.
You said to the foolish, “Do not act foolishly,” and to the wicked, “Do not lift up your horn.”
Do not raise your horn high or speak with your neck held high.
For rising does not come from the west, nor from the wilderness of the mountains.
For God is the judge: he brings one down and raises another up.
For a cup is in the LORD's hand, full of a mixture of wine [?]. He pours it from this one to that one. [?] All the wicked of the earth will drain it and drink.
But I will live forever and sing praises to the God of Jacob.
I will cut off all the horns of the wicked, but the horns of the righteous will be raised.
God is known in Judah, and his name is great in Israel.
May his shelter be in Salem and his dwelling in Zion.
There he broke the arms of the bows, the weapons, and the sword in battle.
You are radiant and anointed, from your mighty mountain.
All the foolish of heart were thrown into confusion. The mighty men slept their sleep and could not find their hands.
At your rebuke, God of Jacob, the horsemen fell asleep.
You are fearsome. Who can stand before you in this anger?
You made judgment heard from heaven; the earth saw and was afraid.
When God rises to judge and to save all the poor of the earth.
For human thought will praise you, and you will remove the rest of his anger [?] wrath.
Make vows and fulfill them to the Lord your God. Let all who surround him bring offerings to the Fearsome One.
He humbles the spirit of rulers and is feared by the kings of the earth.
I cried aloud to God, and he heard me. I raised my voice to him, and he answered me.
On the day of my distress I sought the Lord. His hand struck me through the night without ceasing, and there was no comforter for my soul.
I remembered God and was troubled; I pondered, and my spirit was overwhelmed.
[?] seized me in my eyes. I became speechless and did not speak.
I considered the days of old and the years of ages past.
I remembered and meditated at night. I pondered in my heart, examined my spirit, and said:
“Has the Lord forgotten me forever? Will he never again be pleased with me?
Or will he take his kindness away from me forever? Or will he bring his word to an end for all generations?”
Has God forgotten to show mercy, or has he withheld his compassion in his anger?
I said, “This is my weakness, and these are [?] of the right hand of the Most High.”
For I remembered your wonders from long ago.
I meditated on all your works and reflected on your deeds.
God, your way is holy, and no one is as great as our God.
You are the God who worked wonders and made your strength known among the nations.
With your arm you redeemed your people, the descendants of Jacob and Joseph.
The waters saw you, God; the waters saw you and were afraid. Even the depths trembled.
The clouds dripped water; the highest heavens gave their voice. Your arrows also flew.
The sound of your thunder was in the whirlwinds. Your lightning lit up the world; the earth shook and trembled.
Your way was through the sea, and your paths through the mighty waters, but your footprints were not known.
You led your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
My people, listen to my teaching, heed it, and turn your ears to the words of my mouth.
For look, I will open my mouth in parables and tell of marvels from long ago.
What we have heard, we know—also what our ancestors told us.
We will not hide them from their children, but will tell the coming generation of the LORD’s praiseworthy deeds, his power, and the wonders he has done.
He established his testimony in Jacob and set his law in Israel, as he commanded our ancestors to make them known to their children.
So that the next generation may know—the children who will be born and will rise to tell their children.
So that they would put their hope in God, not forget God’s works, and keep his commandments.
And not be like their ancestors, an evil and rebellious generation, a generation whose heart was not steadfast and whose spirit did not trust in God.
The descendants of Ephraim, who drew the bowstring and shot with the bow, turned back on the day of battle.
Because they did not keep God’s covenant and refused to follow his law.
They forgot his works and the wonders he had shown them.
He worked wonders before their ancestors in the land of Egypt and in the fields of Zoan.
He split the sea and brought them across, and he made the waters stand like wineskins.
He led them by a cloud during the day and by the light of fire all night.
He split the rock in the wilderness and gave them water to drink as from the great deep.
He brought streams out of the rock, and water flowed like rivers.
Yet the people continued to sin and to provoke the Most High in the parched land.
They tested God in their hearts by asking for food for themselves.
They grumbled against God and said, “Can God set tables for us in the wilderness?”
“If he struck the rock and water flowed, and he made streams run, can he also give us bread or prepare food for his people?”
Therefore the Lord heard and became angry. Fire broke out against Jacob, and anger rose against Israel,
because they did not believe in God or trust in his salvation.
He commanded the clouds above, and the doors of heaven were opened.
He sent down manna for them to eat and gave them bread from heaven.
Human beings ate the bread of angels, and he sent them provisions in abundance.
He made winds blow in the heavens and drove the south wind by his strength.
He sent down meat for them like dust, and winged birds like the sand of the seas.
They fell within their camps, all around their tents.
They ate and were fully satisfied, and he gave them what they craved.
They had not turned away from their cravings, and while their food was still in their mouths,
God’s anger rose against them. He killed some of their wealthy men and brought down the chosen men of Israel.
Despite all this, they sinned and still did not believe in his wonders.
They spent their days in futility, and their years passed swiftly.
Whenever he killed them, they sought him; they returned and eagerly sought him.
They remembered that God was their helper, and God Most High their redeemer.
They loved him with their mouths, but with their tongues they lied to him.
Their hearts were not steadfast toward him, and they were not faithful to his covenant.
But he is merciful: he forgives sins and does not destroy. He repeatedly turns away his anger and does not stir up all his wrath.
He remembered that they were flesh, a breath that goes away and does not return.
They embittered him in the wilderness and angered him in the wasteland.
They turned again to testing God and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
They did not remember his hand or the day when he redeemed them from the oppressor,
when he performed his signs in Egypt and his wonders in the fields of Zoan.
He turned their rivers and streams into blood, so that they could not drink the water.
He sent swarms of insects upon them, which devoured them, and frogs, which ravaged them.
He gave their crops to the locust and the fruit of their labor to the caterpillar.
He shattered their vines with hail and their fig trees with frost.
He handed their livestock over to hail and their possessions to fire.
He sent upon them the fury of his anger—fury, wrath, and distress—sent through an evil angel.
He opened up evil paths and did not spare their souls from death; he handed their animals over to death.
He killed all the firstborn of Egypt, the first of all their offspring in the dwelling of Ham.
He led his people out like sheep and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.
He settled them in hope, and they were not afraid; the sea covered their enemies.
He brought them to his holy territory, to this mountain that his right hand had acquired.
He destroyed nations before them and allotted them portions of his inheritance, and the tribes of Israel settled in their tents.
They tested and provoked God Most High, and did not keep his decrees.
They turned back and acted falsely like their ancestors; they turned aside like a treacherous bow.
They angered him with their high places and provoked his jealousy with their idols.
God heard and became furious; he was very angry with Israel.
He forgot the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent where he had dwelt among human beings.
He gave his people over to captivity and his glory into the oppressor’s hand.
He handed his people over to the sword and disregarded his inheritance.
Fire consumed their troops, and their virgins were ravaged.
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows were not mourned.
The Lord awoke as though from sleep, like a man roused by his wine.
He struck his enemies back behind him and gave them everlasting disgrace.
He rejected the tent of Joseph and took no pleasure in the tribe of Ephraim.
He chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loved.
He built his sanctuary on the heights and established it on the earth forever.
He chose David his servant and took him from the flock of sheep.
And from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd Jacob his people and Israel his inheritance.
He shepherded them with integrity of heart and guided them with skillful hands.
God, the nations have entered your inheritance and defiled your holy temple. They have made Jerusalem a ruin.
They have given the corpses of your servants as food to the birds of the sky, and the flesh of your righteous ones to the wild animals of the earth.
They have poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there is no one to bury them.
We have become a disgrace to our neighbors, an object of ridicule and mockery to those around us.
How long will you be angry, Lord? Forever? Will your anger burn like fire?
Pour out your anger on the nations that do not know you, and on the kingdoms that do not call on your name.
For they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his dwelling.
Do not remember our former sins against us. Let your mercy quickly come to meet us, for we have been brought very low.
Help me, God our Savior, for the glory of your name. Forgive me and deliver me from our sins for your name's sake.
Do not let the nations say, “Where is their God?” Let vengeance for the blood of your servants that has been shed be made known among the nations before our eyes.
Let the prisoner's groaning come before you. By the greatness of your arm, free the children from death.
Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their laps for the insults they have hurled at you, Lord.
Then we, your people and the flock of your pasture, will thank you forever. From generation to generation we will recount your wonders.
Shepherd of Israel, listen, and lead Joseph like a flock. You who sit enthroned upon the cherubim, reveal yourself.
Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, show your might and come to save us.
Mighty God, restore us. Make your face shine, and we will be saved.
Lord, mighty God, how long will you be angry at the prayer of your servant?
You have fed them bread with tears and given them tears to drink.
You have made us a byword among our neighbors, and our enemies ridicule us.
Mighty God, restore us. Make your face shine, and we will be saved.
You brought a vine out of Egypt; you destroyed nations and planted it.
You looked after it and planted its root, and the land was filled with it.
The mountains were covered by its shade, and its branches spread over the cedars of God.
It sent its tendrils as far as the sea, and its shoots over the rivers.
Why have you broken down its fence, so that everyone passing along the road tramples it?
The boar from the forest devours it, and the wild animals graze on it.
Mighty God, turn and look down from heaven; see and tend this vine.
And the stock that your right hand planted, and the son of man whom you strengthened for yourself.
Burn its shoots with fire, and let them perish at the rebuke of your face.
Let your right hand be upon the man, and upon the son of man whom you strengthened for yourself.
So that we may not turn away from you, give me life, and we will call on your name.
Lord, mighty God, restore us; make your face shine, and we will be saved.
Praise God, who strengthens us, and shout to the God of Jacob.
Take up tambourines and sweet-sounding harps, together with lyres.
Sound the horns at the new moons and at the full moons, on the days of the festivals.
For this is a law for Israel and a decree of the God of Jacob.
He established it as a testimony in Joseph when he went out to the land of Egypt. He heard a language he did not know.
I removed the yoke from his shoulder and freed his hands from bondage.
In distress he called to me, and I rescued him. I sheltered him in my glorious hiding place and tested him at the waters of contention.
Listen, my people, and I will speak. Israel, I will testify against you, if you will listen to me.
You shall have no foreign god, and you shall not bow down to another deity.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt. Open your mouth, and I will fill it.
But my people did not listen to my voice, and Israel would not be persuaded by me.
They followed the desires of their hearts and their own thinking.
If only my people had listened to me and Israel had walked in my ways!
I would soon have destroyed their enemies and turned my hand against those who hated them.
Those who hated the Lord lied to him, and their trembling lasted forever.
He fed him with the finest wheat and satisfied him with honey from the rock.
God stands in the assembly of angels, and among the angels he will judge.
How long will you judge unjustly and show favor to the wicked?
Give justice to orphans and the unfortunate; vindicate the poor and the lowly.
Rescue the poor and the afflicted from the hand of the wicked.
For they did not know or understand that they were walking in darkness, and all the foundations of the earth shook.
I said, “You are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High.”
Yet you will die like human beings and fall like one of the rulers.
Rise up, God, and judge the earth, for you will inherit all the nations.
God, who is like you? Do not be silent or still, God.
For look, your enemies are in an uproar, and those who hate you have lifted their heads.
In their cunning they have devised a secret plan against your people and plotted against your holy ones.
They said, “Come, let us destroy them as a people, so that the name of Israel will no longer be remembered.”
For they have agreed together in their hearts and made a covenant against you:
the tents of Edom, the Arabs, Moab, and the Gadarenes;
the territory of Ammon, Amalek, and Philistia, together with the inhabitants of Tyre.
The Assyrians also joined them, and they became a help to the descendants of Lot.
Do to them as you did to Midian, to Sisera, and to Nabin at the Kishon River,
who were destroyed at Endor and became manure on the ground.
Lay them waste and destroy them like Oreb, Zeeb, Zebah, and Zalmunna—all their rulers.
They said, “Let us take possession of God's dwelling for ourselves.”
God, make them like a rolling wheel and like stubble before the wind.
Like a fire let loose in a forest, and like a flame that burns the mountains,
so pursue them with your whirlwind and throw them into confusion with your hailstorms.
Fill their faces with disgrace, so that they will seek your name, Lord.
Let them be ashamed and terrified forever and ever; let them be disgraced and perish.
Let them know that your name is the LORD; you alone are exalted over the whole earth.
How lovely are your dwellings, mighty Lord!
My soul has waited and longed for the courts of the Lord. My heart and my flesh have praised the living God.
Even the sparrow has found a home for herself, and the turtledove a nest. They have raised their young beside your altar, mighty Lord, my King and my God.
Blessed are those who live in your house; they will praise you forever.
Blessed is the person whose helper you are, and in whose heart are your paths.
They passed through the valley of weeping and made it a dwelling place. The lawgiver will also be clothed in blessing.
They will go from strength to strength, and the God of gods will appear in Zion.
LORD, mighty God, hear my prayer; listen, God of Jacob.
Look, O God our helper, and gaze on the face of your anointed one.
For one day in your courts is better than a thousand. I would rather live in the house of God than live in the tents of the wicked.
For the LORD God is our sustainer and helper. The LORD will give mercy and honor, and he will not withhold his good things from those who walk with integrity.
LORD, mighty God, blessed is the person who trusts in you.
You took pleasure in your land, LORD, and brought back the captives of Jacob.
You forgave your people's wrongdoing and covered all their sins.
You removed all your fury and turned away your fierce anger.
Restore us, God our Savior, and put an end to your anger against us.
Do not be angry with us forever, and do not keep your anger through generation after generation.
Instead, restore me and bring me to life, so that your people may rejoice in you.
Show me your grace, LORD, and give us your salvation.
Let us hear what the LORD our God says, for he speaks peace to his people and to his righteous ones, so that they will not turn back.
His salvation is near to those who fear him, so that his glory may dwell in our land.
Grace and truth have met me; righteousness and peace will kiss.
Faithfulness will spring up from the earth, and righteousness has looked down from heaven.
The LORD will also give his good things, and the earth will yield its crops.
The righteous person will walk before him and set his footsteps on the earth.
Incline your ear, LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and afflicted.
Protect my life, for you are good. You, O God, save your servant who trusts in you.
Have mercy on me, LORD, for I call to you every day.
Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, LORD, I have lifted up my soul.
For you, LORD, are good, and your grace is abundant toward all who call on you.
Listen to my prayer, Lord, and hear my cry.
On the day of my distress I called to you, and you answered me.
There is no one like you, Lord our God, and there are no works like yours.
All the nations you have made will come and worship you, Lord, and glorify your name.
For you are great and do wonderful things; you alone are God.
Show me your way, Lord, and I will walk in truth. Let my heart rejoice with those who fear your name.
I will thank you, Lord my God, with all my heart, and glorify your name forever.
For your kindness toward me is great, and you have rescued my soul from the depths of Sheol.
God, wicked people have risen against me, and a gathering of powerful men has sought my life. They have not remembered you.
But you, Lord, are a merciful and compassionate God, slow to anger and abundant in kindness and faithfulness.
Turn toward me and have mercy on me. Give strength to your servant, and save the son of your servant woman.
Show me a sign of favor, so that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, because you, Lord, have helped and comforted me.
His foundations are on his holy mountain.
The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things have been spoken of you, city of our God.
I will remember Rahab and Babylon among those who know me. Look, Philistia and Tyre and the people of Cush: this one was born there.
And of Zion it was said, “A mighty man was born in her,” and he himself established her.
The Lord will count the peoples in a register: “This one was born there.”
The nobles who live in you will rejoice, and so will all who have been humbled in you.
Lord, God of my salvation, I have cried out by day and by night before you.
Let my prayer come before you; incline your ear to my plea.
For my soul is filled with troubles, and my life has drawn near to Sheol.
I was counted among those who go down to the pit, and I became like a man who has no strength.
I am free among the dead, like the slain who lie in graves, whom you no longer remember and who are lost from your hands.
You have brought me down into the lowest pit, into darkness and the shadows of death.
Your anger weighs upon me, and you have brought all your waves upon me.
You have taken my acquaintances far from me and made me unclean to them. I am shut in and cannot go out.
My eye has wasted away from my affliction. I have called on you, Lord, every day and stretched out my hands toward you.
Will you perform wonders for the dead? Will the mighty rise and give thanks to you?
Will those in the graves recount your goodness, or your faithfulness in destruction?
Will your wonder be known in the darkness, or your righteousness in the land that has been forgotten?
But I have cried out to you, Lord, and in the morning my prayer will come before you.
Do not forget my soul, Lord, and do not turn your face away from me.
I am wretched and weary from my youth. I have been raised up, brought low, and bewildered.
Your anger has passed over me, and your terrors have silenced me.
They have surrounded me like water all day long and have come against me together.
You have taken my loved ones and companions far from me, and you have separated my acquaintances from me.
I will sing of the Lord’s goodness forever, and with my mouth I will make his faithfulness known from generation to generation.
For he said that the world will be built by grace, and that you will establish your faithfulness in the heavens.
I have made a covenant with my chosen one and sworn to David my servant:
I will establish your descendants forever and build your throne from generation to generation.
The heavens will give thanks for your wonders, Lord, and for your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones.
Who in the highest heavens can compare with the Lord? Who among the sons of angels is like the Lord?
God stands in the assembly of the holy ones, great and awesome above all who surround him.
Lord, mighty God, who is powerful like you? Your faithfulness surrounds you.
You rule over the swelling of the sea, and you still the tumult of its waves.
You bring the proud low like the slain. With your mighty arm you have scattered your enemies.
The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours. You established the world and all that fills it.
You created the north and the south. Tabor and Hermon praise your name.
Yours is the arm, and yours is the might. May your hand be strong and your right hand be raised.
Your throne is established in righteousness and justice. Goodness and truth go before you.
Blessed are the people who know your praises, Lord. They will walk in the light of your face.
They will rejoice in your name all day long, and through your righteousness they will be exalted.
For you are the glory of our strength, and by your favor our horn will be raised.
For the Lord is our trust, and the Holy One of Israel is our king.
Then he spoke in visions with his righteous ones and said, “I have given help to a man and raised up a chosen one from the people.
I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him.
My hand helped him, and my arm strengthened him.
His enemy did not prevail against him at all, and no wicked man humbled him.
I will destroy his enemies before him and shatter those who hate him.
My faithfulness and my grace are with him, and in my name his horn will be raised high.
I will set his hand over the sea and his right hand over the rivers.
He will call to me, ‘You are my Father, my God, and my mighty Savior.’
I too will make him the firstborn and raise him above the kings of the earth.
I will preserve my grace for him forever, and my covenant with him will stand firm.
I will establish his descendants forever, and his throne for as long as the heavens endure.
If his sons abandon my law and do not walk in my commandments,
I will punish their wrongdoing with a rod and their sins with blows.
But I will not withdraw my grace from him or prove false to my faithfulness.
I will not reject my covenant or change what has gone out from my lips.
Once I swore to David by my holiness, and I will not lie:
His descendants will endure forever, and his throne will be like the sun before me.”
Like the moon, it will be established forever, a faithful witness in the heavens.
But you have forgotten me and rejected me, and you have turned away the face of your anointed one.
You have rejected the covenant with your servant and thrown his crown to the ground.
You have broken down his fences and demolished his strongholds.
All who pass along the road have trampled him, and he has become an object of scorn to his neighbors.
You have raised the right hand of his enemies and made all who hate him rejoice.
You have turned back the help of his sword and have not supported him in battle.
You have brought his champions to nothing and thrown his throne down to the ground.
You have shortened the days of his youth and covered him with shame.
How long will you be angry, Lord? Forever? Will your anger burn like fire?
Remember me in the pit, for you did not create all human beings in vain.
Who can live without seeing death, or rescue himself from the power of Sheol?
Where are your former acts of kindness, Lord, which you swore to David in your faithfulness?
Remember, Lord, the disgrace of your servant: throughout my life I have borne all the murmuring of the nations.
Your enemies have mocked me, Lord, and they have mocked the footsteps of your anointed one.
Blessed is the Lord forever. Amen and amen.
Lord, you have been our dwelling place throughout our generations.
Before the mountains were conceived, before the earth went into labor, and before the world was established, from everlasting to everlasting you are God.
You have brought humanity back to humiliation and said, “Return, human beings.”
For a thousand years in your eyes are like yesterday when it has passed, and like a watch in the night.
Their generations will be sleep, and in the morning they will pass away like grass.
In the morning it sprouts and grows anew, and in the evening it withers and dries up.
For we have been consumed by your anger and troubled by your wrath.
You have set our sins before you, [?] in the light of your face.
For all our days have ended under your anger, and our years have ended like a spider’s web.
The days of our years amount to seventy years, and at most eighty years. Most of them are toil and pain, for humiliation has come upon us, and we have been shaken.
Who knows the strength of your anger and the terror of your wrath?
Make known to me the number of our days, so that we may gain a wise heart.
Turn back, Lord! How long will you leave your servants without comfort?
Satisfy me in the morning with your kindness, so that we may give praise and rejoice all our days.
Make us glad because [?] our wrongdoing, and the years in which we saw evil.
Let your works be seen by your servants, and your splendor upon their children.
May the kindness of the Lord our God be upon us. Establish the work of his hands for us, and make us firm through the work of his hands.
He who lives in the shelter of the Most High is glorified in the shadow of God.
Say to the Lord, “My confidence and my refuge, my God in whom I trust.”
For he will rescue you from the snare that makes you stumble and from empty speech.
With his feathers he will rescue you, and under his wings you will take shelter. His truth will surround you like armor.
Do not fear the terror of the night or the arrow that flies by day,
or the word that walks in darkness, or the spirit of the demon at noon.
Thousands will fall at your side, and tens of thousands at your right hand, but they will not come near you.
You will only look with your eyes; you will see the punishment of the wicked.
For you, Lord, are my confidence, you who have set your dwelling on high.
Evil will not approach you, and no affliction will come near your tent.
For he will command his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.
They will carry you in their arms so that you do not stumble with your foot.
You will tread on the asp and the viper, and trample the lion and the dragon.
Because he has sought me, I will rescue him and strengthen him, because he knows my name.
He will call on me, and I will answer him. I am with him in distress; I will strengthen him and honor him.
I will satisfy him with a long life and show him my salvation.
It is good to give thanks to the LORD and to sing praises to your name, Most High.
To proclaim your kindness in the morning and your faithfulness at night.
I will play a ten-stringed harp, and I will play a lyre.
For you have made me glad, Lord, through your deeds, and I will glory in the work of your hands.
How great are your works, Lord, and how very deep are your thoughts!
A stupid person does not know, and a fool does not understand this:
When the wicked sprout like grass and all who do evil flourish, it is so that they may perish forever and ever.
But you, Lord, are exalted forever.
For look, your enemies, Lord—for look, your enemies will perish, and all who do evil will be scattered.
You have raised my horns like those of a wild ox and drenched me with fragrant oil.
My eyes have seen my enemies, and my ears will hear about the wicked who rise against me.
The righteous will flourish like a palm tree and grow tall like the cedars of Lebanon.
Those planted in the Lord’s house will flourish in the courts of our God.
They will continue to grow in old age; they will be vigorous and flourishing.
They will declare that the Lord, the Mighty One, is upright, and there is no injustice in him.
The Lord reigns and is clothed in majesty. The Lord has clothed himself in strength and made himself strong. He has established the world so that it will not be shaken.
Your throne has been established from ancient times, and you are from eternity.
The rivers have risen, Lord; the rivers have raised their voices; the rivers have risen in purity.
Mightier than the sound of many waters are the sea’s breakers; the Lord is glorious on high.
Your testimonies are utterly trustworthy. Holiness befits your house, Lord, for all time.
God of vengeance, Lord, God of vengeance, reveal yourself!
Rise up, Judge of the earth, and repay the proud!
How long will the wicked, Lord, how long will the wicked boast?
They bluster and speak injustice; all who do evil speak out.
They have humbled your people, Lord, and enslaved your inheritance.
They have killed widows and foreign residents and destroyed orphans.
They say, “The Lord does not see; the God of Jacob pays no attention.”
Understand, you senseless people! You fools, how long will you fail to understand?
Does the one who planted the ears not hear? Does the one who created the eyes not perceive?
Does the one who disciplines the nations not rebuke—the one who teaches human beings knowledge?
The Lord knows human thoughts, that they are empty.
Blessed is the person whom you discipline, Lord, and teach from your law.
You give him relief from evil days until a pit is dug for the wicked.
For the Lord will not abandon his people or forsake his inheritance.
For judgment returned to the righteous, and all the upright in heart followed him.
Who will rise up for me against the wicked? Who will stand ready for me against those who do evil?
If the Lord had not been my helper, my soul would soon have dwelt in misery.
I said, “My feet are slipping,” and your kindness, Lord, supported me.
When the pains of my heart multiplied, your consolations rescued my soul.
A throne of unjust rulers cannot be allied with you; they fashion injustice against your law.
They lie in wait to hunt down the life of the righteous and condemn innocent blood.
The Lord became my strength, and the mighty God my helper.
He turned their injustice back upon them and silenced them in their wickedness; the Lord our God silenced them.
Come, let us praise the Lord and sing to our God, our Savior.
Let us come before him with thanksgiving and praise him with songs.
For the Lord is a great God, a king greater than all gods.
In his hands are the foundations of the earth and the heights of the mountains.
The sea is his, and he made it; his hands formed the dry land.
Come, let us kneel and worship him, and bless the Lord who made us.
For he is our God, and we are his people and the sheep of his pasture. Today, if you hear his voice,
do not harden your hearts to provoke him, as those who rebelled did, as on the day of testing in the wilderness,
when your ancestors tested me and put me to the test, though they saw my works.
For forty years I was weary of that generation, and I said, “They are a people whose hearts have gone astray, and they have not known my ways.”
So I swore in my anger, “They will not enter my rest.”
Sing a new song of praise to the Lord; praise the Lord, all the earth.
Praise the Lord and bless his name; proclaim the good news of his salvation day after day.
Tell of his glory among the nations, and of his deeds among all peoples.
For our Lord is great and greatly to be praised, and he is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the nations are worthless, but the Lord made the heavens.
Splendor and glory are before him; strength and praise are in his sanctuary.
Give to the Lord, families of the nations; give to the Lord praise and honor.
Give the Lord the honor due his name; bring offerings and enter his courts.
Worship the Lord in his holy court; let all the earth tremble before him.
Say among the nations, “The Lord reigns.” He has established the world so that it will not be shaken. He will judge the peoples fairly.
Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad. Let the sea rejoice with all that fills it.
Let the fields flourish, and everything in them. Then let all the trees of the forest sing praise.
Before the Lord, who comes to judge the earth. He judges the world with righteousness and the peoples with faithfulness.
The Lord reigns. Let the earth be glad; let the many islands rejoice.
Clouds and thick darkness surround him. His throne is established in righteousness and justice.
Fire will devour before him and burn up his enemies.
His lightning lit up the world. The earth saw it and trembled.
The mountains melted like wax before the Lord, the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens proclaimed his righteousness, and all the peoples saw his glory.
Let all who make idols and boast in carved images be ashamed. Worship him, all his angels.
Zion will hear and rejoice, and the daughters of Judah will be glad because of your judgments, Lord.
For you, Lord, are exalted above all the earth, and you are raised far above all gods.
Those who love the Lord hate evil. He guards the lives of his righteous ones and will rescue them from the hand of the wicked.
Light dawns for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.
Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous, and give thanks as you remember his holiness.
Sing a new song of praise to the Lord, for he has done a marvelous thing. His right hand and his holy arm have saved him.
The Lord has made his salvation known and revealed his righteousness before the eyes of the nations.
He remembered his kindness and his faithfulness to the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
Praise the Lord, all the earth. Rejoice, sing, and give praise.
Sing to the Lord with harps and with the sound of song.
With the sound of horns, give praise before the King, the Lord.
Let the sea surge with all that fills it, the world and its inhabitants.
Let the rivers clap their hands together, and let the mountains sing praise.
Before the Lord, who comes to judge the earth. He judges the world with righteousness and the peoples fairly.
The Lord reigns; let the peoples tremble. He sits enthroned upon the cherubim; let the earth shake.
The Lord is great in Zion and exalted above all peoples.
Let them give thanks to your great and awesome name, for it is holy.
The king’s strength loves justice. You have established fairness; you have carried out justice and righteousness in Jacob.
Exalt the Lord our God and bow down at his footstool. He is holy.
Moses and Aaron were among his priests, and Samuel among those who called on his name. They called to the Lord, and he answered them.
He spoke with them in the pillar of cloud. They kept his testimony and the covenant he gave them.
Lord our God, you answered them. You were an avenging God to them; repay them according to their deeds.
Exalt the Lord our God and bow down at his holy mountain, for the Lord our God is holy.
Praise the Lord, all the earth.
Serve the Lord with joy; come before him with praise.
Know that he is the Lord our God. He made us, and not we ourselves. We are his people and the sheep of his pasture.
Enter his gates with thanksgiving and his courts with praise. Give thanks to him and bless his name.
For the Lord is good; his kindness lasts forever, and his faithfulness through every generation.
I will sing of kindness and justice; to you, Lord, I will sing praise.
I will walk in your blameless way. How long until you come to me? I have walked within my house with integrity of heart.
I have set nothing wicked before my eyes. I have hated the one who does evil, and he has not attached himself to me.
An evil heart has departed from me, and I have not known evil.
I would destroy anyone who secretly slandered his neighbor. I would not eat with anyone whose eyes were haughty and whose heart was proud.
My eyes are on the faithful of the land, so that they may live with me. Whoever walks in a blameless way will serve me.
No one who practices deceit will live within my house, and no one who speaks lies will remain before my eyes.
In the morning I will silence all the wicked of the land and destroy all evildoers from the city of the Lord.
Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.
Do not turn your face away from me on the day of my distress, but incline your ear to me. On the day I call to you, answer me quickly.
For my days have vanished in smoke, and my bones have turned white like firebrands.
My heart has been scorched like grass and has dried up, for I have forgotten to eat my bread.
Because of my groaning, my flesh clings to my bones.
I have become like a pelican in the wilderness, like an owl among the ruins.
I stayed awake and was alone, like a bird flitting about on the rooftops.
All day long my enemies taunted me, and those who praised me swore by me.
For I ate ashes like bread and mixed my drink with tears,
because of your fury and anger, for you lifted me up and threw me down.
My days have declined like a shadow, and I have withered like grass.
But you, Lord, endure forever, and your remembrance lasts through all generations.
Arise and have mercy on Zion, for the time has come to have mercy on her.
For your servants delight in her stones and love her dust.
The nations will fear your name, Lord, and all the kings of the earth your glory.
For the Lord has built Zion and appears in his glory.
He turns toward the prayer of the poor and does not despise their prayer.
Let this be written for a coming generation, and let a people yet to be created praise the Lord.
For he looked down from his holy height; the Lord looked from heaven to earth,
to hear the prisoner's groaning and to release children from death,
so that they may proclaim the Lord's name in Zion and his praises in Jerusalem,
when the peoples gather together, and the kingdoms, to serve the Lord.
They weakened my strength on earth, and in the brevity of my days.
He said to me, "Do not take me away halfway through my days; your years last through all generations."
Long ago you established the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They pass away, but you endure. They all wear out like clothing and are changed like a worn-out cloth.
But you remain as you are, and your years do not end.
The children of your servants will dwell in the land, and their descendants will be established before you.
Bless the Lord, my soul, and let all my bones bless his holy name.
Bless the Lord, my soul, and do not forget all his benefits.
He forgives all your wrongdoing and heals all your diseases.
He redeems you from destruction and sustains you with grace and mercy.
He satisfies your body with good things and renews your youth like an eagle's.
The Lord acts righteously and gives justice to all the oppressed.
He makes his ways known to Moses and his deeds to the children of Israel.
The Lord is merciful and compassionate, slow to anger and abundant in kindness.
For he is not angry forever, nor does he hold on to his anger forever.
For he has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our wrongdoing.
For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is the Lord’s kindness toward those who fear him.
And as far as the east is from the west, so far will he remove our wrongdoing from us.
And as a father has compassion on his children, the Lord has compassion on those who fear him.
For he knows how we were formed; he remembers that we are dust.
A human being’s days are like grass; like a blossom in the field, so he flourishes.
For when the wind blows over it, it is gone, and its place is no longer known.
The Lord’s kindness is from eternity to eternity toward those who fear him, and his righteousness extends to their children’s children,
to those who keep his covenant and remember his commandments and carry them out.
The Lord has established his throne in heaven, and his kingdom rules over everything.
Bless the Lord, you his angels, mighty in strength, who carry out his commandments.
Bless the Lord, all his armies and his servants who do his will.
Bless the Lord, all his works throughout the whole earth under his rule. Bless the Lord, my soul.
Bless the Lord, my soul. The Lord my God is very great; he is clothed in splendor and majesty.
He clothed himself in light like a garment; he stretched out the heavens like a tent curtain.
He made his dwelling places in the waters, set his chariot upon the clouds, and walks upon the wings of the wind.
He makes his angels winds, and his servants burning fire.
He established the earth on its foundations, so that it will never be shaken.
The deep covered it like a garment, and the waters stood above the mountains.
At your rebuke they flee, and at the sound of your thunder they hurry away.
They went up the mountains and down the valleys to the place you prepared for them.
You set a boundary for them, so that they would not cross it and cover the earth.
He sends springs into the valleys, and they flow between the mountains.
They give water to every wild animal, and the thirsty wild donkeys drink their fill.
The birds of the sky dwell above them; from among the mountains they raise their voices.
He waters the mountains from his dwelling places; the earth is satisfied with the fruit of your works.
He makes grass grow for livestock, and plants for people to cultivate, to bring forth bread from the earth.
Wine gladdens a person’s heart, and oil makes his face shine; bread strengthens a person’s heart.
The Lord’s trees will drink their fill, and the cedars of Lebanon that he planted.
There the birds nest, and the stork has its nest in the cypresses.
The high mountains are for the wild goats, and the cliffs are a refuge for the rock badgers.
He made the moon to mark the seasons, and the sun knows the time of its setting.
He made darkness, and it became night; in it all the animals of the forest dwell.
The lions roar for prey and seek their food from God.
When the sun rises, they gather together and lie down in their dens.
People go out to their work and to their labor until evening.
How many are your works, Lord! You made them all with wisdom, and the earth is full of your possessions.
Here is the sea, great and wide, in which are countless swarming creatures, animals both large and small.
There the ships sail, and there is Leviathan, which you created to make sport of.
They all wait for you to give them food at the proper time.
You give to them, and they are nourished; you open your hand, and they are satisfied.
You turn your face away, and they are troubled; you take away their breath, and they die and return to their dust.
You send your spirit, and they are created, and you renew the face of the earth.
May the glory of the Lord endure forever; may the Lord rejoice in his works.
He looks at the earth, and it trembles; he rebukes the mountains, and they smoke.
I will praise the Lord throughout my life, and I will sing to my God as long as I exist.
May my praise be pleasing to him, and I will rejoice in the Lord.
May sinners perish from the earth, and may the wicked no longer remain in it. Bless the Lord, my soul.
Give thanks to the Lord and call on his name; make his deeds known among the nations.
Praise him and sing to him; recount all his wonders.
Praise his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice.
Seek the Lord and be strengthened; seek his face at all times.
Remember the wonders he has done, his wonders and the judgment of his mouth.
You descendants of Abraham his servant, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is the Lord our God; his judgments are throughout the earth.
He remembers his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
the covenant he established with Abraham, and his oaths to Isaac.
And his testimony with Jacob, a covenant for Israel forever.
And he said, “To you I will give the land of Canaan, the allotted portions of their inheritance.”
When you were few in number, just a few, and were living in it,
they traveled from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another people.
He allowed no one to oppress them; he rebuked kings on their behalf:
“Do not come near my anointed ones, and do not harm my prophets.”
He called down a famine on the land and broke every stalk of their grain.
He sent a man ahead of them: Joseph was sold into slavery.
He bound his feet in fetters, and he himself was put in irons.
Until his word was fulfilled, the word of the Lord tested him.
The king sent and released him; he made him ruler over his people.
A master over his household and a ruler over all his possessions,
to discipline rulers as he wished and teach wisdom to elders.
Israel entered Egypt, and Jacob lived in the dwelling place of Ham.
He greatly increased his people and made them stronger than their enemies.
They turned their hearts to hate his people and to plot against his servants.
He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron, whom he had chosen.
He performed his signs among them, and his wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness and made it dark, and they rebelled against his word.
He turned their waters into blood and killed their fish.
He made frogs swarm in their land and in the chambers of their kings.
He spoke and brought swarms of flies and lice throughout their territory.
He turned their rain into hail, and fire blazed in their land.
He struck their vines and fig trees and shattered the trees throughout their territory.
He spoke and brought locusts and countless caterpillars throughout their land.
They ate all the vegetation and the fruit of their lands.
He killed all the firstborn of Egypt, the first of all their offspring.
He brought them out with silver and gold, and no one among their tribes was sick.
Egypt rejoiced when they left, because fear of them had fallen upon the Egyptians.
He spread a cloud over them and shaded them, and fire to give light at night.
They asked, and he brought them food and satisfied them with bread from heaven.
He opened the rock, and water flowed out; water ran through a thirsty land.
For he remembered his holy promise to Abraham his servant.
He brought his people out with joy, his companies with songs of praise.
He gave them the lands of the nations, and they inherited the fruits of the peoples’ labor.
So that they would observe his commandments and keep his laws.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, and his kindness lasts forever.
Who can recount the wonders of the Lord and proclaim all his praises?
Blessed are those who keep his judgments and practice his righteousness at all times.
Remember me, Lord, with the favor you show your people, and save me with your salvation.
So that I may see the good things of your chosen ones, rejoice in your joy, and glory in your inheritance.
We have sinned along with our ancestors; we have done wrong and acted wickedly.
Our ancestors in Egypt did not understand your wonders and did not remember your many acts of kindness; they rebelled at the waters, at the Red Sea.
Yet he saved them for his name’s sake, to show his mighty power.
He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up; he led them through the depths as through a wilderness.
He saved them from the hand of the enemy and rescued them from the hand of the oppressor.
The waters covered their oppressors; not one of them remained.
They believed his words and sang his praises.
They quickly forgot God and did not wait for his counsel.
They craved intensely in the wilderness and put God to the test in the desert.
He granted them their requests and sent satisfaction to their souls.
They were jealous of Moses in the camp, and of Aaron, the Lord’s holy one.
The earth opened and swallowed Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram.
Fire blazed among their companies, and a flame burned up the wicked.
They made a calf at Horeb and worshiped a cast-metal image.
They exchanged their glory for the image of an ox that eats grass.
They forgot God, who saved them, who did great things in Egypt.
And wonders in the land of Ham, and awe-inspiring deeds at the Red Sea.
He said he would destroy them, had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him and turned back his anger so that he would not destroy them.
They rejected the desirable land and did not believe his word.
They grumbled in their tents and did not obey the voice of the Lord.
He raised his hand against them, swearing to destroy them among the nations,
and to scatter their descendants among the nations and destroy them in other lands.
For they joined themselves to the idols of Peor and ate sacrifices offered to the dead.
They angered him by their deeds and made him jealous with their idols, and suddenly the plague grew severe among them.
Phinehas stood up and prayed, and the plague was stopped.
This was counted to him as righteousness for all generations, forever.
They angered him at the waters of strife, and Moses suffered because of them.
Because they embittered his spirit and spoke with his lips.
They did not destroy the nations as the Lord had told them,
but mingled with the nations and learned their practices.
They worshiped their idols, which became a snare to them.
They sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons.
They shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan, and the land was defiled with blood.
They defiled themselves by their deeds and prostituted themselves through their practices.
The Lord's anger burned against his people, and he rejected his inheritance.
He handed them over to the nations, and those who hated them ruled over them.
Their enemies enslaved them, and they were subjected to their power.
Many times he rescued them, but they embittered him with their schemes and were brought low because of their wrongdoing.
He saw their distress and heard their plea.
He remembered his covenant and had compassion on them, and he led them according to his abundant kindness.
And he granted them compassion in the sight of all their captors.
Save us, Lord our God, and gather me from the nations, so that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your inheritance.
Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Let all the people say, “Amen and amen.”
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, and his kindness lasts forever.
Let those redeemed by the Lord say so, whom he redeemed from the hand of the oppressor.
He gathered them from all the lands, from the east and the west, from the north and the sea.
They wandered in the desolate wilderness and could not find a road to an inhabited town.
They were hungry and thirsty, and their souls grew faint.
They pleaded with the Lord in their troubles, and he brought them out of their distress.
He led them along a path of truth, to go to inhabited towns.
Let his righteous people give thanks to the Lord, for his compassion is upon humankind.
For he satisfied weary souls and filled the hungry soul.
Of those who sit in darkness and in the shadows of death, imprisoned in poverty and in iron chains.
Because they rebelled against the word of God and rejected the counsel of the Most High,
he broke their hearts with hardship. They grew weak, and there was no one to help them.
They prayed to the Lord in their distress, and he saved them from their troubles.
He brought them out of darkness and the shadows of death and cut through their bonds.
Let his righteous people give thanks to the Lord, for his compassion is upon humankind.
For he broke the bronze gates and cut through the iron bars.
He helped them out of the path of their sins, and they were humbled because of their wrongdoing.
Their souls loathed all food, and they drew near to the gates of death.
They pleaded with the Lord in their troubles, and he brought them out of their distress.
He sent his word and healed them, and delivered them from destruction.
Let his righteous people give thanks to the Lord, for his compassion is upon humankind.
Offer him sacrifices of praise; praise his deeds in his wonders.
Those who go down to the sea in ships and make crossings on the mighty waters—
they saw the deeds of the Lord and his wonders in the depths of the sea.
For he raised a storm wind, and the waves of the sea rose high.
They rise to the heavens and descend to the depths, and their souls are shaken within them.
They reeled and staggered like drunkards, and all their wisdom vanished.
They cried out to the Lord in their distress, and he brought them out of their troubles.
He calmed the storm, and the waves of the sea fell silent and came to rest.
They rejoiced when the waves fell silent, and he led them to the harbor they desired.
Let his righteous ones give thanks to the Lord for his mercies toward humanity.
Praise him in the assembly of the peoples, and exalt him in the council of the elders.
For he turned rivers into a wilderness and springs of water into thirsty ground.
He turned land that yielded its fruit into a salt wasteland because of the evil deeds of its inhabitants.
For he turned the wilderness into pools of water and thirsty ground into springs of water.
He settled the hungry there, and they built towns and lived in them.
They sowed fields and planted vineyards, and ate the fruit of their harvests.
He blessed them, and they multiplied greatly; he did not diminish their livestock.
They dwindled and were brought low through great adversity and sorrow.
He cast calamity upon rulers and made them wander in a trackless wasteland.
He strengthened the poor and made their families like a flock.
So that the righteous may see and rejoice, and all the wicked may shut their mouths.
Whoever is wise, let him observe these things and understand the Lord’s steadfast love.
My heart is ready, O God; my heart is ready. I will praise and sing with my glory.
Awake, my harp! Awake, lyre and harp! And I will awake at dawn.
I will give thanks to you among the peoples, God, and sing to your name among the nations.
For your goodness is great, reaching to the heavens, and your faithfulness to the highest heavens.
Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and let your glory be over all the earth.
So that your beloved ones may be delivered, save me with your right hand and answer me.
God has spoken in his holiness: “I will rejoice; I will divide Shechem and measure out the Valley of Succoth.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine. Ephraim is the protection of my head; Judah is my king.
Moab is my washbasin; over Edom I will cast my sandals, and over Philistia I will shout.”
Who will bring me to the fortified city, and who will lead me as far as Edom?
For look, you, O God, have forgotten us, and you do not go out with our armies.
Give us strength against our enemies, for human help is worthless.
God will give us strength, and he will trample our enemies.
O God of my praise, do not be silent.
For the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful have opened against me; they have spoken to me with a lying tongue.
With a voice of hatred they fought against me without cause.
In return for my love they opposed me, while I prayed for them.
They repaid me with evil for good, and hatred for love.
Appoint a wicked person over them, and let an accuser stand at their right hand.
When they are judged, let them come out guilty, and let their prayer count as sin.
Let their days be few, and let others take what is reserved for them.
Let their children become orphans and their wives widows.
Let a creditor lay claim to everything they have, and let strangers plunder their wealth.
May they have no one to show them mercy, and may no one have mercy on their orphans.
Let their end be destruction, and let their name be blotted out in the next generation.
Let the wrongdoing of their fathers be remembered, and let the sins of their mothers not be blotted out.
Instead, let them remain before the Lord at all times, and let him destroy their memory from the earth.
For they did not remember to do good, but persecuted the poor, the afflicted, and the brokenhearted to death.
They loved curses and did not desire blessings.
They put on curses like armor; these entered them like water and went into their bones like oil.
Let it be to them like a ragged garment they wrap themselves in, and like a belt always around their waist.
This is the work of those who oppose the Lord and of those who speak evil against my life.
But you, Lord, act on my behalf for your name's sake; because your kindness is good, rescue me.
For I am poor and miserable; my heart is troubled within me.
My steps have faltered like a declining shadow, and I have been shaken off like a locust.
My knees have grown weak from fasting, and my flesh has wasted away for lack of oil.
I became an object of scorn to them; they saw me and shook their heads.
Help me, LORD my God, and save me according to your grace.
Let them know that this is your doing, and that you have done it.
